article.title: Israel’s targeted assassinations continue across Gaza despite the US-backed ceasefire
article.author: Aseel Saleh
article.content: Israel escalated its aggression across the Gaza Strip during the last few days, carrying out targeted assassinations of senior Hamas officials and a United Nations employee. On Monday, November 23, an employee of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA) was killed in an Israeli drone strike while on duty in the Jabalia Refugee Camp in the northern Gaza Strip. On the same day, an Israeli warplane struck a civilian vehicle near Ansar Roundabout, west of Gaza City, killing three people and injuring several others. On the following day, Israel killed the head of the internal security service in the northern Gaza Strip, Mohammad Abu al-Ouf (48), alongside his wife, Noura Abu al-Ouf (42) , and two daughters, Yusra (15) and Jana (13) , in an airstrike on an apartment in Al-Shati refugee camp in western Gaza City. In a statement on Tuesday, Hamas denounced the assassination of security officials in Gaza, stressing that the attacks aim to spread chaos in the war-ravaged territory. The resistance movement cautioned that these targeted killings are intended to destabilize Palestinian society and its internal security, and constitute part of Israel’s “genocidal tools against civilians and civilian infrastructure in the Gaza Strip.” For many, the Israeli escalation across Gaza has once again exposed Tel Aviv’s endeavors to torpedo the US-brokered ceasefire deal , which was reached in October 2025 but violated on a daily basis by the Israeli military. Media reports surfaced on Tuesday, citing senior advisor to Trump’s Board of Peace, Josh Gruenbaum, accusing Israeli Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of obstructing the implementation of the deal and the roadmap that stemmed from it. Read more: Cryptocurrency, billions of dollars, and five countries to send troops: what’s new in Trump’s “Board of Peace” for Gaza Gruenbaum further praised Netanyahu’s political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, who was tasked with forming the new Israeli government earlier in the month, for being “highly supportive” of pushing the process ahead.
